long_biography.plain_text:
Before committing large sums to Genentech, venture capitalist Tom Perkins and his colleagues paid outside researchers to test the scientific questions on which the young biotechnology company depended. His approach put modest amounts of capital against the most consequential technical uncertainties first. Larger investment could follow once experiments had established that an idea was workable.

The partnership's obligations to its investors mattered to him too. At Kleiner Perkins, he helped establish rules against partners making personal investments that could compete with the fund's interests. Even shares received for serving on company boards went into the partnership. He also favoured returning profits to investors promptly, giving each fund a clear conclusion instead of continually reinvesting its proceeds.
